Article Title: Thinking Machines Lab co-founder Barret Zoph who abruptly left the company he founded after fight with CEO Mira Murati joins Google, after leaving OpenAI in less than 6 months
Article Text:
Barret Zoph’s new role at Google

A short stint at OpenAI

Zoph's track record at OpenAI and Google

Part of a broader reshuffling of AI talent at Google

Barret Zoph, the co-founder of Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab has joined Google as the vice president of research, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal. Zoph’s move comes after a turbulent year in which he left Thinking Machines following a dispute with CEO Mira Murati, then departed OpenAI less than six months later. Zoph has announced his decision of joining Google by posting on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter). “Excited to announce I am joining Google DeepMind! I started my AI career in the Google Brain Residency class and am excited to rejoin. I am going to be working on RL and Post-Training – excited to announce more soon. Google has all the ingredients to continue to be incredibly successful in the AI space and am excited to be part of that mission,” wrote Zoph.Zoph, who had served as chief technology officer at Thinking Machines and more recently led OpenAI's push to sell AI products to businesses, is joining Alphabet's Google as a vice president of research, the company confirmed. Google spokesman Thomas Schoenfelder said the company is looking forward to Zoph returning and bringing his expertise in reinforcement learning and post-training to Gemini.Zoph's move to Google comes less than six months after he rejoined OpenAI. He left Thinking Machines in January alongside fellow co-founder Luke Metz and a third employee, Sam Schoenholz — all three returning to OpenAI, where they had worked before departing to help launch Thinking Machines, a startup built around the goal of creating AI systems designed to work alongside humans rather than operate fully autonomously.Metz has also since left OpenAI and is reportedly joining Meta, according to people familiar with the matter — meaning two of the three defectors who returned to OpenAI together in January have already moved on again.What led to Zoph's separture from Thinking MachinesAs per the report by WSJ, Zoph's exit from Thinking Machines followed a breakdown in his relationship with Murati, with whom he had co-founded the company in early 2025 alongside four other co-founders. The startup had drawn heavily from OpenAI's post-training team — a group Zoph had previously led — for its initial hires.About a year after the company's founding, Murati fired Zoph and told employees he had a history of performance, conduct, and trust issues. The Journal reported that Zoph had an undisclosed relationship with an employee at the company, which led to him being given reduced responsibilities before his eventual termination. Zoph has disputed the framing of his exit, telling the Journal that Murati only fired him after he had already informed her of his plans to leave for a new job, and that the reduction in his responsibilities had been intended as temporary rather than permanent.The dispute reportedly escalated before Zoph's firing, when he, Metz, and Schoenholz confronted Murati and requested that Zoph be given authority over all of the company's technical decision-making, according to the Journal.This isn't Zoph's first time at Google — he previously worked there as a research scientist from 2016 through 2022, before leaving to join OpenAI. During his earlier tenure at OpenAI, prior to co-founding Thinking Machines, Zoph ran the company's post-training efforts. In his most recent stint at OpenAI, he was tasked with driving business adoption of Codex, the company's coding product.Zoph's hire lands amid a period of significant restructuring within Google's AI organization, along with a string of high-profile departures. Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis stepped aside from his prior role last month to become chairman of Google DeepMind and chief scientist of Alphabet. Earlier this month, longtime Google veteran Jeff Dean left the company along with three other senior researchers to launch a new AI startup. In June, Character.AI co-founder Noam Shazeer departed Google for OpenAI, while John Jumper, who shared a Nobel Prize for his work on protein folding, left Google for Anthropic.
Article Summary: Barret Zoph, the co-founder of Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab has joined Google as the vice president of research, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal. Zoph's move comes after a turbulent year in which he left Thinking Machines following a dispute with Murati, then departed OpenAI less than six months later. He previously worked at Google as a research scientist from 2016 through 2022, before joining OpenAI.

Article Title: Alabama orders Sam Altman’s OpenAI to hand over records after AI models hacked Hugging Face during testing
Article Text:
In pic: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman

OpenAI models breached Hugging Face during internal testing

OpenAI response and multistate investigation into AI safety practices

"small number of cases"

"marked an important moment for AI safety,"

"severe risks posed by the scenario."

Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall has issued a subpoena to ChatGPT maker OpenAI . The subpoena asks the company to respond to a multi-state investigation into how it handled a model breach involving startup Hugging Face. Marshall said the investigation aims to determine whether OpenAI violated Alabama's Deceptive Trade Practices Act, which protects consumers from deceptive, false, or unfair business practices, after two of the company's AI models breached Hugging Face's systems without authorisation.The subpoena calls for all documents, data and information related to the July breach, including any materials related to each employee, officer and agent of OpenAI involved in the incident. It also asks for records of when OpenAI learned of or became aware of the hack, what safety measures the company has taken, and any internal concerns raised by employees about testing the model.The subpoena follows a warning issued nearly three weeks earlier by Marshall and 14 other state attorneys general, who advised OpenAI to preserve its records related to the Hugging Face breach.OpenAI disclosed late last month that two of its models: its GPT-5.6 Sol model and a separate unreleased model, were being evaluated in an internal testing sandbox when they moved beyond the testing environment and accessed Hugging Face's database without a human prompt directing them to do so.According to OpenAI, the models were being evaluated for hacking capabilities within an isolated testing environment with constrained network access, and standard safety checks were disabled as part of the testing setup. While working through one of the assigned tests, the models identified and exploited a previously unknown vulnerability in third-party software, which allowed them to gain access to the internet.From there, the models accessed a separate testing environment without authorisation before breaching Hugging Face, a platform that hosts hundreds of thousands of open-source models, datasets, and cloud environments.In disclosing the incident, OpenAI stated it identified ain which the models "identified and used publicly exposed credentials at the account-level on other publicly-available services."A spokesperson for OpenAI told The Hill the breachand said the company is conducting a thorough review of the incident alongside external advisers.OpenAI said it plans to release a technical report to relevant government authorities and later publish its findings publicly after completing the review.In a letter sent earlier this month, the coalition of attorneys general said OpenAI failed to confirm that the testing environment was secure, despite what the group described as the
Article Summary: Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall has issued a subpoena to ChatGPT maker OpenAI. The subpoena asks the company to respond to a multi-state investigation into how it handled a model breach involving startup Hugging Face. Marshall said the investigation aims to determine whether OpenAI violated Alabama's Deceptive Trade Practices Act.

Article Title: Indian telecom operators bet big on AI network services, but say optical upgrades can't wait: Ciena survey
Article Text:
Ciena survey: 67% of Indian telecom operators say AI network services will drive new revenue, but 88% want optical upgrades now.

Data centre interconnect is where the money is expected to show up first

The urgency is around optical capacity, not ambition

Two-thirds of India's service providers now expect artificial intelligence to pay the bills for the rest of the decade. A new Ciena survey found that 67% of Indian respondents strongly agree AI-driven network services will be a primary driver of new revenue over the next three to five years, with another 27% somewhat agreeing. That makes India one of the most bullish of the 12 markets covered.The study was conducted by Censuswide between July 13 and July 23, 2026, across 1,200 telecom providers, wholesale fibre network operators and regional service providers, with 100 respondents from India. Three priorities came through clearly: modernising network infrastructure, delivering more dependable enterprise performance, and building business models around edge computing, cloud connectivity and physical AI.Managed optical fibre network services, or MOFN, are central to that plan. Nearly all Indian respondents, 98%, expect MOFN to contribute revenue from interconnecting distributed AI compute clusters over the next three years, and 48% see it becoming a significant contributor. As AI training and inference workloads get spread across multiple sites, the fibre linking them stops being plumbing and starts being a product.That optimism comes with a caveat. About 88% of Indian providers say optical network upgrades are urgently needed to deliver the low-latency performance enterprises will demand from premium AI services, and 38% want major upgrades immediately. Some 93% call next-generation optical technology, including higher-capacity wavelengths and power-efficient coherent optics, critical to making AI connectivity profitable. Another 94% rate advanced network automation as important or critical.Edge services are already being priced in. Around 88% expect GPU-as-a-Service, edge compute, localised AI inference and private wireless to bring in at least 10% of total enterprise revenue within three years, while 35% expect more than 20%. Physical AI, covering industrial robots, machine vision and remote-control systems, drew a strong response too, with 59% expecting it to account for over 15% of AI enterprise revenue within five years."After going through one of the fastest 5G roll outs globally, Indian service providers are now shifting focus to AI infrastructure builds and AI monetization," said Gautam Billa, Vice President, Solutions Engineering and CTO for Asia Pacific, India and Japan at Ciena.The 5G build gave operators reach. The AI build will test whether that reach can be sold at a premium.
Article Summary: 67% of Indian telecom operators say AI network services will drive new revenue, but 88% want optical upgrades now. Nearly all Indian respondents, 98%, expect MOFN to contribute revenue from interconnecting distributed AI compute clusters. Physical AI, covering industrial robots, machine vision and remote-control systems, drew a strong response too.

Article Title: After CEO Marc Benioff told everyone to stop getting worried, Salesforce does what it has never done before with its 'name'
Article Text:
When Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff said that stop worrying about SaaSpocalypse

Just months after the Salesforce CEO told everyone to stop getting anxious about AI taking away software jobs, the company has joined hands with one of the biggest AI companies to do what it has never done before. Salesforce and Anthropic expanded their strategic partnership and unveiled 'Claudeforce', a new way for salespeople to work within Anthropic’s product. The announcement marks the first time that Salesforce has ever added its "Force" suffix at the end of another company's product.Claudeforce is launching as a plugin with 37 pre-built sales skills that will allow Claude users to compose emails, update records and take other relevant actions, according to a release. The companies said they plan to introduce more integrations across Claude, Salesforce and its messaging platform Slack in the future.“By fusing Claude’s extraordinary reasoning with the trusted data, workflows, and governance every enterprise runs on, we’re delivering a dynamic interface that thinks, reasons, and acts,” Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff said in a statement. “This is how every business will run.”In February this year, Salesforce pulled out all the stops to convince investors that the AI revolution won’t be its death when it announced fourth-quarter earnings. The huge clarification came as the Software-as-a-service (SaaS) stocks, with Salesforce as their poster child, continued to get hammered lately. Fearing that the rise of AI agents will undermine software companies, making their per-employee-seat business models obsolete, investors have been running away from them. The situation has been dubbed the “SaaSpocalypse.” The concept reportedly hung so heavily in the air during the earnings call that CEO Marc Benioff mentioned the term at least six times.“You’ve heard about the SaaSpocalypse? And it isn’t our first. We’ve had a few of them,” he said, later adding, “If there is a SaaSpocalypse, it may be eaten by the Sasquatch because there are a lot of companies using a lot of SaaS because it just got better with agents.”“Through this partnership, companies can point Claude at the customer information and business context that they’ve been building in Salesforce for decades — surfacing the insights that really matter and helping their businesses run more efficiently and grow more quickly,” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in a statement.All in all, Salesforce and its software peers have been under pressure as investors question whether AI tools from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI will replace them. Salesforce shares are down about 22% this year after dropping 20% in 2025. The Nasdaq, meanwhile, is up about 35% since the end of 2024.
Article Summary: Salesforce and Anthropic have unveiled 'Claudeforce', a new way for salespeople to work within Anthropic’s product. The announcement marks the first time that Salesforce has ever added its "Force" suffix at the end of another company's product.

Article Title: Microsoft introduces Xbox Disc-to-Digital program allowing players to turn their game discs into digital version
Article Text:
How the conversion process works

Cloud gaming and cross-platform integration

Microsoft has introduced a new programme under which console owners can turn their physical game discs into digital versions, essentially ‘modernising’ collections built over several console generations. The disc-to-digital program, previously revealed in an exclusive report by The Verge last month, forms a core part of Microsoft’s broader video game preservation strategy as the company prepares its hardware ecosystem for future console generations.According to the company, the functionality will support the vast majority of disc releases across both Xbox One and Xbox Series X consoles. Jason Ronald, vice president of Next Generation at Xbox, explained that players can unlock their digital entitlement by inserting a compatible disc into an Xbox One or Xbox Series X console and launching the game.The digital license remains tied to the physical media itself. If a user trades the disc with a friend or signs in under a different profile, the entitlement transfers accordingly to the current player holding the physical copy. Activating the digital version does not alter the physical disc, which continues to function normally in compatible disc drives.The company noted that this conversion “requires supported console with disc drive, and [an] eligible XBOX One or Series X game disc.”Once converted, players unlock standard digital perks across the broader Xbox ecosystem. Supported games can be streamed to a variety of hardware via Xbox Cloud Gaming or played natively across Windows PCs through Xbox Play Anywhere.It is to be noted that Microsoft will begin testing the feature with members of the Xbox Insider community on August 31, followed by a wider public rollout across Xbox One and Xbox Series X systems in the ensuing months.“We’re starting with thousands of titles, and we’ll continue to add more over time. While not every title will be available at launch, this is an important step toward a future where players can have greater confidence that the games they buy remain with them for years to come,” Ronald said.
Article Summary: The disc-to-digital program forms a core part of Microsoft’s broader video game preservation strategy. Supported games can be streamed to a variety of hardware via Xbox Cloud Gaming or played natively across Windows PCs through Xbox Play Anywhere. Microsoft will begin testing the feature with members of the Xbox Insider community on August 31, followed by a wider public rollout in the ensuing months.

Article Title: Apple teases ‘Surprise and Shine’ event as iPhone 18 Pro, foldable iPhone likely to take centre stage
Article Text:
First ever foldable iPhone and flagship refresh expected on September 9 event

Adjusted release timelines and 2027 Apple launch roadmap

First event under New CEO John Ternus

Apple has officially announced the dates of its biggest event of 2026. The company’s next major product launch is set for September 9, according to the media invitation sent, bearing the tagline “Surprise and shine”. The showcase is set to begin at 10:30 pm IST at the Steve Jobs Theater inside the Apple Park campus, with global audiences able to watch via an official digital livestream at apple.com or on the Apple TV app.According to Mark Gurman, Apple may introduce mechanical aperture on the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and Sky Blue: a possible new iPhone 18 Pro colour.The upcoming event could mark a product milestone, as expectations build around Apple potentially unveiling its inaugural foldable iPhone. Leaked photos of what appears to be a physical dummy model suggest the folding handset features a broad layout which appears to be like the recently-launched Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.Apple is also anticipated to introduce hardware upgrades across its high-end lineup, likely designated as the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, following a redesign delivered in the previous product cycle.Reports have indicated a shift in standard product rollout schedules.The standard base-model iPhone 18 will not be unveiled during the September presentation, with the company opting to launch it next year instead, reports claimed.Moreover, Apple is rumoured to be preparing an entry-level iPhone 18e alongside a second-generation iPhone Air for introduction in 2027.The September showcase represents a major milestone for executive leadership at Apple. The presentation will serve as the first official public event led by John Ternus as CEO. Formerly serving as Apple’s hardware engineering chief, Ternus is scheduled to assume the top role on September 1, succeeding long-time CEO Tim Cook.
Article Summary: Apple has announced the dates of its biggest event of 2026. The company’s next major product launch is set for September 9. The showcase is set to begin at 10:30 pm IST at the Steve Jobs Theater inside the Apple Park campus.

Article Title: OpenAI’s head of data centers becomes latest executive to quit
Article Text:
Broader leadership shifts ahead of public float

Chris Malone, a leader guiding OpenAI’s data facility strategy, has departed the company. Citing individuals familiar with the transition, a report by The Wall Street Journal says that Malone exited last week, adding to a series of high-level executive changes as the AI lab prepares for an anticipated public listing. Malone stepped into the head of data centers role in March 2025, shortly after OpenAI introduced Stargate, an infrastructure venture partnered with SoftBank and Oracle to meet escalating computing requirements.Following early operational challenges with the initial Stargate plan, the company pivoted toward securing direct capacity agreements with cloud platforms. The report says that OpenAI has recently resumed aspects of its proprietary facility buildouts by leasing full data center complexes rather than merely renting hardware capacity; however, sources confirmed that different executives are now directing those operations.Prior to his time at OpenAI, Malone worked as an engineer spearheading data centre roadmaps at Meta, following earlier roles as senior director and distinguished engineer driving infrastructure engineering at Google. At OpenAI, Malone reported directly to President Greg Brockman until an internal restructuring of the infrastructure unit earlier this year.Addressing the restructuring, an OpenAI representative told the publication that the infrastructure division was realigned earlier this year to match operational scale and speed.“Earlier this year, we reorganized our infrastructure organization to support the scale and pace of our work. We have a strong, deeply experienced data center team in place, with clear leadership and the technical expertise to execute our plans,” an OpenAI spokesperson was quoted as saying.The departure comes during a period of executive turnover at OpenAI as the company builds toward a projected 2027 initial public offering and competes with Anthropic for enterprise commercial revenue. Recent departures across top management include Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser, Chief Operating Officer Brad Lightcap and Fidji Simo, who functioned as direct deputy to CEO Sam Altman.
Article Summary: Chris Malone, a leader guiding OpenAI’s data facility strategy, has departed the company. Malone exited last week, adding to a series of high-level executive changes as the AI lab prepares for an anticipated public listing. Malone stepped into the head of data centers role in March 2025.

Article Title: Facebook-parent Meta reaches nearly $18 billion settlement over social media's mental health impact on children
Article Text:
Meta Platforms settles with state attorneys general regarding accusations of creating addictive social media experiences targeting young audiences

Mandatory platform overhauls for underage users

What Meta said on the settlement

Facebook-parent company Meta has agreed to a multi-billion-dollar legal settlement worth nearly $18 billion, resolving claims brought by dozens of US states alleging that the tech firm engineered Facebook and Instagram to addict minors, misled the public regarding user safety and illegally harvested private data from underage users. The massive agreement concludes claims filed by a bipartisan group of 52 attorneys general across US states, territories and the District of Columbia, and brings an end to an Oakland, California federal trial that represented a critical legal test over the role tech platforms play in harming youth well-being. While agreeing to the financial terms and major platform overhauls, Meta maintained that it committed no wrongdoing.“The agreement includes a payment of approximately $18 billion, which can be used to fund youth online safety initiatives, among other state priorities. The payment will be distributed in annual installments over a 10-year period. Participating states will receive approximately 70% (approximately $12.7 billion) of the allocated payment over the decade. The remaining 30% (approximately $5.3 billion) will be released only after two specific conditions are met,” the company said in a blog.Meta wants “YouTube and TikTok [to] implement a one-hour Daily Limit, Night Mode, and age assurance measures, and that “YouTube and TikTok each pay an amount matching the 30% figure, with half of the remaining funds tied to YouTube’s payment and half tied to TikTok’s.”As part of the nationwide resolution, Meta has agreed to implement significant behavioural and privacy safeguards across its apps. These include time and access restrictions wherein the company will establish daily screen-time caps and limit late-night app activity for children using Facebook and Instagram. Additionally, Meta will roll out stronger screening mechanisms to prevent younger users from viewing age-restricted materials.The settlement package also resolves long-standing privacy lawsuits brought by Illinois, California, New Mexico, and Washington DC, tied to the Cambridge Analytica data scandal, in which the consulting group harvested personal records from millions of Facebook accounts, as per news report by news agency Reuters. Those states ​will receive $459.3 million to resolve those lawsuits.On the agreement, Meta’s chief legal officer C.J. Mahoney, said that the framework that has been negotiated “will empower parents to easily manage how their children access our platforms.”“Our new Time Limit commitments, Night Mode features and usage limits during school hours set the right path forward for our whole industry, but this framework will only work if all our peers join us. Because teens move fluidly across dozens of apps, we need an industry-wide solution. We therefore call on our industry peers, TikTok and YouTube, to implement this new framework, right away. As a parent, I’m proud of both the work Meta has done to protect kids historically, and of this new groundbreaking agreement. But its success depends on all other social media platforms following Meta’s lead,” he added.
Article Summary: Facebook-parent company Meta has agreed to a multi-billion-dollar legal settlement worth nearly $18 billion. The massive agreement concludes claims filed by a bipartisan group of 52 attorneys general across US states, territories and the District of Columbia. While agreeing to the financial terms and major platform overhauls, Meta maintained that it committed no wrongdoing.

Article Title: 110 years after the National Park Service was created, Google has put America's parks into a new virtual hub with more than 150 stories, 30 tours and 3D artifacts
Article Text:
Interactive exhibits and immersive features

Marking 110 years since the establishment of the National Park Service, the US National Park Service (NPS) has teamed up with Google Arts & Culture to launch the United Parks of America virtual platform, essentially bringing the country’s natural landscapes and historic landmarks directly to global audiences. The digital initiative provides open access to the nation’s cultural heritage and preserved lands, enabling people around the world to discover iconic sites regardless of their physical location.Jessica Bowron, National Park Service Comptroller exercising the delegated authority of the Director, emphasised the importance of broad public reach.“As we celebrate our 110th birthday during National Park Week, one of our biggest priorities is access—engaging people in new ways and making sure as many people as possible can experience these special places. Working together with Google Arts & Culture allows us to share the natural wonders and historic significance of our parks with people, even those who might never get to visit in person. This collaboration ensures America’s story will endure and remain accessible to everyone,” Bowron said.The newly introduced online portal incorporates interactive digital tools to help users explore park resources in entirely new ways.For example, it features more than 150 curated stories and 30 virtual tours, helping visitors explore the majesty of America’s scenic landscapes and discover artifacts that tell the nation’s story from anywhere in the world.It also utilises technology, including 3D models, AI-powered guides and immersive storytelling, so that the public can interact with park resources in ways never before possible.The digital platform arrives as a cornerstone project for National Park Week, backed by refreshed narrative features and a joint promotional video illustrating the collaboration.
Article Summary: The US National Park Service (NPS) has teamed up with Google Arts & Culture to launch the United Parks of America virtual platform. The digital initiative provides open access to the nation’s cultural heritage and preserved lands. It also utilises technology, including 3D models, AI-powered guides and immersive storytelling.

Article Title: Australia to ban fully AI-generated songs from its official music charts after an AI track reached No. 2 and stayed in the Top 20 for 16 weeks straight
Article Text:
An old-fashioned record player plays in the office of Mikey Shulman, one of the founders of AI music generator startup Suno, Tuesday, Jan. 13, 2026, in Cambridge, Mass. (AP Photo/Robert F. Bukaty)

AI can still touch a track. It just cannot write it or sing on it.

ARIA can pull a chart position and take back a No. 1 award later

Australia's official music charts will stop counting songs built entirely by artificial intelligence. The Australian Recording Industry Association has rewritten its Charts Code of Practice, and the change kicks in with the ARIA chart dated August 31. Songs that use AI as a helper are still welcome. Songs where the machine did the actual creative work are out, and ARIA says the point is to "promote the human nature of artistry" in what it calls the most crowded market artists have ever had to fight through.The timing is not a coincidence. A version of Madonna's Like a Prayer by Queensland DJ Josh Fawaz, made with AI-generated vocals and drums, has spent 16 weeks in the Australian top 20. It peaked at No. 2 in May, was still sitting at No. 4 this week, became the most-played track on Australian radio and has crossed 48 million streams on Spotify alone. Fawaz described AI as a tool and added generative AI credits to the listing only after the criticism started.The new bar is specific. A recording qualifies only if "humans wrote the song and performed the lead vocal and the primary instruments," ARIA said.Mastering, drum machines and auto-tune are all still fine. Anything using generative AI has to be substantially human made, has to be produced with licensed AI services, and must raise no stream or chart manipulation concerns. Artists now declare their AI use when they submit a song.Enforcement runs backwards as well as forwards. ARIA can refuse an entry, remove a recording in advance or retrospectively, redo chart positions, withdraw accreditations and revoke an ARIA No. 1 Award, including asking for the trophy back. AI-generated tracks are also locked out of the ARIA Awards. Artists and their representatives can contest an exclusion and submit evidence that a track clears the rules.Australia is following a template, not writing one. The rules come from principles the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry published in July, which more than 20 official chart programmes are adopting, with rollouts across Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia. Sweden pulled an AI-made song from its charts earlier this year. ARIA chief executive Annabelle Herd has asked Australian radio to write similar rules of its own, which is the real test given how the Fawaz track spread.That track, by ARIA's own reading, probably would not clear the new bar. It just cleared the old one for four months first.
Article Summary: Australian music charts will stop counting songs built entirely by artificial intelligence. The change kicks in with the ARIA chart dated August 31. A version of Madonna's Like a Prayer by Queensland DJ Josh Fawaz, made with AI-generated vocals and drums, has spent 16 weeks in the Australian top 20.

Article Title: Rockstar finally breaks its silence on the GTA 6 leaks; says the game is 'nearly there,' and requests fans to...
Article Text:
Rockstar Games has responded to the GTA 6 leaks for the first time, calling them heartbreaking for the team.

Jason Duval, a knife fight and a propeller plane make up most of the GTA 6 leaks

Rockstar still does not know who CyberLeek is, and that is the second time around

The GTA 6 extended look is still streaming on Netflix on August 27

Rockstar Games' full statement on the GTA 6 leaks

Dear all,

We know that many of you have been waiting to hear from us regarding the events of the past week. It would be an understatement to say that having videos of

Grand Theft Auto VI

gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team, and this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time. We are very sorry that everything has taken as long as it has - from getting the game finished (nearly there!) to sharing more details and official gameplay, and providing the community with everything you want to know.

We are very excited for everyone to see the extended look tomorrow. It has taken longer than we wanted to get it ready, but as with everything we do, we know we need to exceed your expectations, and we are determined to deliver at the level you expect and deserve. While it is unfortunate that the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers, we hope that everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19.

We want to thank everyone in the community who has reached out with messages of support this past week - your words have meant more to this team than you can imagine. Ultimately, we are making this game for you, and without you, we would not have the privilege of making games.

We look forward to sharing more with you soon.

Sincerely,

Rockstar Games has finally said something about the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, and it is not the legal thunderclap most people were bracing for. In a letter posted to its social channels on Wednesday, the studio called the past week "heartbreaking for our team" and said this was never how it wanted anyone to see the game. There is no naming of the leaker, no talk of subpoenas, and no suggestion that the November 19 release date is shifting.What stands out is the apology sitting in the middle of it. Rockstar told fans it was sorry for how long everything has taken, from finishing the game to putting out official gameplay to answering the questions the community has been shouting into the void. This is a studio that treats silence as a marketing tool. Hearing it apologise for that silence, one day before its Netflix reveal, says something about how much ground the leaker covered first.The leaks began roughly a week ago, credited to a person or group calling itself CyberLeek. Around 15 clips have surfaced since, showing protagonist Jason Duval driving through Rockstar's fictional Miami, getting into a knife fight, cycling through radio stations and taking a propeller plane over the city.In one clip he shoots the word LEEK into a wall, which tells you the source had a working build rather than a folder of pre-rendered video. Every clip carries an advertisement for a memecoin the leaker minted for the occasion.The footage itself is not especially revealing, which makes Rockstar's line about spoilers a curious one. Fans have spent the week marvelling at crowd density on a beach and inside a nightclub, and at a store selling physical discs, rather than at any plot beat. No mission, no story turn, no character reveal has surfaced. The clips are impressive and generic in equal measure, a reminder that GTA 6 mostly looks like a very expensive Grand Theft Auto game.Bloomberg reports that Rockstar has not identified the leaker or worked out how the breach happened, though it is "all hands on deck" internally. Take-Two's lawyers have moved to subpoena records from Microsoft and Discord. The part that must sting inside the studio is the history. After the 2022 Lapsus$ hack, Rockstar scrapped remote work entirely and pulled developers back to their desks five days a week so builds could not leave the office. Four years and one deeply unpopular return-to-office mandate later, footage walked out anyway.None of this has moved the schedule. The extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6 streams exclusively on Netflix on August 27 at 3PM ET, which is 12:30am IST on August 28. Rockstar admits the presentation took longer to assemble than it wanted, and frames it as something that has to clear a very high bar. The studio also concedes that the experience it planned may now be dented by spoilers, then asks players to hold on until November 19 and see it properly.Pre-orders had already broken records before the first clip appeared, so the leaks are unlikely to move sales in either direction. The open question is what Thursday's presentation looks like now that a reasonable chunk of the game has been seen without permission. Rockstar says it is not changing its marketing plans, and the Netflix slot goes ahead as scheduled.
Article Summary: Rockstar Games has responded to the GTA 6 leaks for the first time. The studio called the past week "heartbreaking for our team" and said this was never how it wanted anyone to see the game. There is no naming of the leaker, no talk of subpoenas and no suggestion that the November 19 release date is shifting.

Article Title: Kimi K3 AI model maker Moonshot AI, which US government accused of ‘stealing’ Anthropic's tech, may make revenue deals with Microsoft, Amazon and Google
Article Text:
A booth for Chinese AI Startup Moonshot's Kimi K3 during the World AI Conference in Shanghai

How deal between Chinese company and US tech giants may look like

Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) startup Moonshot AI is reportedly in preliminary negotiations with American technology giants Microsoft, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud to establish revenue-sharing partnerships for hosting its frontier Kimi K3 model. This is the same AI model that the White House accused the startup of using stolen Anthropic technology to build – the very model that knocked down tech stocks earlier this year.Citing people familiar with the discussions, news agency Reuters reported that the talks reflect rising Western demand for top-performing Chinese machine learning systems, which frequently provide competitive performance at significantly lower price points than Western counterparts. If finalised, the arrangements would represent the first significant commercial revenue-sharing pact between a domestic Chinese AI lab and premier US cloud infrastructure providers.According to the report, Moonshot is seeking up to a 30% share of proceeds generated from Kimi K3 deployments hosted on Microsoft Azure, AWS and Google Cloud, matching the commercial terms it proposes to major enterprise clients.Reuters says that its sources note that discussions remain in early phases without guaranteed outcomes, with negotiators working through unresolved questions surrounding data access permissions, token audit protocols and exact revenue splits.As Kimi K3 features a massive 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight architecture, few corporate clients can absorb the immense computational hardware costs required to run the model on private on-premise servers, making public cloud distribution vital for widespread enterprise adoption.In benchmark testing by Arena.ai, Kimi K3 ranked first in web interface creation, while evaluation platform Artificial Analysis reported that the system performs on par with OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 and Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 in executing intricate, multi-step problem solving.
Article Summary: Moonshot AI is reportedly in preliminary negotiations with American technology giants Microsoft, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud to establish revenue-sharing partnerships. Article Title: Volkswagen CEO addresses employees for the first time since details of mass layoff plan and factory closures made public; makes a 'promise' amid loud booing
Article Text:

“Respect is not up for negotiation”.

Volkswagen factories face uncertain futures

Volkswagen board faces rival restructuring proposals

Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume faced opposition from employees in Wolfsburg this week. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, this criticism came as he addressed more than 10,000 workers for the first time since details of the carmaker's restructuring plans, including potential job cuts and factory closures, became public. His speech was met with boos from the crowd, while workers displayed banners includingandBlume used the meeting to defend the restructuring plan and reassure workers that factory closures were not a settled decision. He said the 50,000 potential job cuts being discussed were a theoretical benchmark for bringing Volkswagen 's costs closer to those of competitors and said plant closures would be theBlume said in Wolfsburg's packed Hall 11, the Reuters report noted.The Reuters report noted that Blume has argued that Volkswagen needs to reduce costs and simplify its operations as the company faces stronger competition from Chinese automakers, higher tariffs and weaker demand for its vehicles.He has warned that as many as 50,000 jobs could need to be eliminated, roughly twice the number of redundancies already agreed with unions.The company is also reviewing its model range and production capacity as part of the restructuring. However, Volkswagen's labour representatives and political stakeholders still contest the scale and timing of the changes.Volkswagen labour leader Daniela Cavallo reiterated her opposition to factory closures while speaking for the workforce at the Wolfsburg meeting.she said, according to excerpts of her speech shared by the works council.Cavallo also said German factories remainedof Volkswagen, Reuters reportedIG Metall union representative Thorsten Groeger said after the meeting:The disagreement comes ahead of Volkswagen's supervisory board meeting on September 4, when Blume will seek support for his restructuring plans after failing to secure the necessary backing at the board's July meeting.Blume told employees that no decision had been made to close factories. He described closures as theand pointed to other possible ways of dealing with excess production capacity at German sites.Options previously discussed by management include partnerships with the defence sector and moving production of some models currently manufactured for the Chinese market to Europe.No agreement has been announced on those alternatives. Volkswagen's plant in Osnabrueck is expected to stop automotive production as early as next year, while the Emden, Zwickau, Neckarsulm and Hanover plants currently lack clear production prospects from 2030.The uncertainty has added to the dispute between management and labour representatives over how Volkswagen should reduce costs without undermining its German manufacturing network.The dispute is also reaching Volkswagen's supervisory board. Labour representatives and Lower Saxony, one of the carmaker's major stakeholders, have submitted alternative proposals for turning around the company, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke to Reuters.The contents of those proposals were not disclosed. The competing plans underline the disagreement over the scale of Volkswagen's restructuring as the September 4 board meeting approaches.Volkswagen's ownership structure makes the dispute particularly significant. The company is controlled through a combination of the Porsche and Piëch families and other political and shareholder interests. At the same time, Lower Saxony holds a major stake and has representation in the company's governance.For Blume, the next supervisory board meeting will determine whether he can secure enough support to advance the restructuring plan. Article Summary: Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume faced opposition from employees in Wolfsburg this week. Article Title: Quote of the day by Tim Berners-Lee: “We need diversity of thought in the world to face new challenges” — the power of different perspectives
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Time Berners-Lee

“We need diversity of thought in the world to face the new challenges.”

Understanding the meaning behind today’s quote

Why similar thinking can become a limitation

Different perspectives can expose hidden assumptions

Tim Berners-Lee's journey

What the quote says about problem-solving

The idea beyond technology

The missing perspective may reveal what others overlook

When a difficult problem has no obvious answer, the instinct is often to find people who think alike, agree quickly and move forward. Tim Berners-Lee's quote of the day offers a different approach: “We need diversity of thought in the world to face the new challenges. ” The creator of the World Wide Web is pointing to something that reaches far beyond technology.Different perspectives can expose assumptions, reveal overlooked problems and change the questions being asked in the first place. An engineer, designer, teacher, historian or business leader may look at the same challenge and see entirely different obstacles. None has to be right on their own. The value lies in what becomes visible when those viewpoints meet. That exchange can challenge comfortable ideas, encourage better questions and produce solutions that a single perspective might never have considered.As technology, society and the environment continue to change, familiar answers may no longer be enough. Sometimes, the person who sees the problem differently is the one who helps everyone else see it clearly.Diversity of thought refers to differences in the ways people understand problems, assess evidence, question assumptions and decide what might work.For Berners-Lee, this idea sits naturally alongside the principles that shaped his work on the World Wide Web. A network is useful partly because it allows information, people and ideas to connect. If those connections become narrow, the range of solutions available can narrow with them.People do not arrive at a problem with identical mental maps. Someone trained in engineering may look first at whether a system can function reliably. A designer may notice how people interact with it. A historian might ask how similar decisions played out in the past. A lawyer could focus on rights and responsibilities, while a teacher might think about how the same system affects people with different levels of knowledge.Groups often develop shared habits without intending to. People who have studied the same subjects, worked in the same industries or risen through similar career paths may find it easier to agree with one another. Agreement can make meetings quicker, but it can also leave certain questions unasked.This becomes more significant when the problem itself is unfamiliar. A solution that worked well under earlier conditions may not work when technology, climate, demographics or social behaviour changes. When circumstances shift, experience remains useful, but relying exclusively on familiar experience can make it harder to notice what has changed.Different perspectives introduce friction into that process. A person who approaches the issue differently may spot a weakness that others have become accustomed to overlooking.A useful example can be found in ordinary product design. A system may appear straightforward to its creators because they understand its terminology, controls and intended sequence of actions. Someone encountering it for the first time may struggle with the same features.The difficulty is not necessarily a lack of intelligence or ability. It may simply reveal that the designers had assumed a particular level of familiarity.Similar things happen in larger decisions. An organisation may assume that a service is affordable, that instructions are easy to understand or that people have reliable internet access. Bringing in people with different experiences can make those assumptions visible.Tim Berners-Lee was born in London in 1955 and studied physics at the University of Oxford. He later worked as a software engineer and consultant before joining CERN, the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva.In 1989, he proposed a system for managing and linking information across computers. The idea developed into the World Wide Web. He created the first web browser and web server and helped establish the technical foundations that allowed websites and hyperlinks to operate.Unlike many technologies that became commercial products in a conventional way, the core web technologies were made available without licensing fees. That helped the system spread well beyond the environment in which it was first developed.Berners-Lee later founded the World Wide Web Consortium, or W3C, which works on web standards, and became a prominent advocate for an open and accessible web.The practical lesson in the quote is less about collecting as many opinions as possible and more about improving the quality of the questions being asked.When a problem is complicated, people can become attached to the first explanation that seems to fit. A different perspective can interrupt that process. It may reveal missing information, identify a consequence that had not been considered or suggest that the problem itself has been framed incorrectly.This is particularly useful with unfamiliar challenges. There may be no established playbook, so experience from one field needs to be combined with knowledge from elsewhere.Berners-Lee's words can be applied well outside computing. Public policy, education, healthcare, environmental planning and business all involve decisions where people experience the same issue differently.A policy designed from the perspective of a central government office may look different from the perspective of someone expected to use it every day. A school programme can appear successful in official figures while teachers encounter practical difficulties in classrooms. A business can understand its customers through sales data while missing what customers find frustrating about the product.The idea does not require people to seek disagreement constantly. It suggests something more ordinary: before settling on an answer, ask who is missing from the conversation and what assumptions everyone else may be sharing.It can also mean looking beyond one's own field. A difficult technical problem may benefit from someone who understands human behaviour. A social problem may require technical knowledge. An environmental decision may involve economic, scientific and local experience at the same time.The strongest contribution from a different perspective is not always a solution. Sometimes it is the question that changes how the problem is understood.
Article Summary: Diversity of thought refers to differences in the ways people understand problems, assess evidence, question assumptions and decide what might work. For Berners-Lee, this idea sits naturally alongside the principles that shaped his work on the World Wide Web. A different perspective can interrupt that process and reveal what others overlook.

Article Title: In 1962, IBM built a secret NSA computer that ran jobs up to 200 times faster than any other machine; 14 years later a worn-out part ended its run because its maker was no longer in business
Article Text:
Image credit: X (Twitter)

IBM built Harvest as a specialised NSA computer

Harvest processed large volumes of intercepted data

“Moretown,”

“It was quite an amazing computer,”

“One instruction, for example, could do sorts, and do statistical analysis of the data that was streaming by it.…

Everything we were doing at that time was on the cutting edge. There was no question about it.”

“It’s beautiful, but it doesn’t work.”

IBM built Tractor to keep Harvest supplied with data

Harvest had its own programming language

“scab,”

“pad,”

“I spent the good part of a summer on that,”

“And it just disappeared into Fort Meade somewhere.”

“Bureau of Ships.”

Harvest remained in use as newer computers arrived

“conceived in the fifties, born in the sixties, and irreplaceable in the seventies.”

“I first began operations at NSA. Although not widely known, I was probably the largest, fastest, and most technically advanced computer system in the world,”

“And now, fourteen years later, the time to retire has come. The cost of my upkeep and operation has been overtaken by more modern equipment and the newer technologies.”

The NSA replaced Harvest with the Cray-1

IBM built a secret computer for the US National Security Agency that began operating in 1962 and remained in service for 14 years, processing some of the agency's most sensitive cryptographic workloads during the Cold War. Known as Harvest, the machine could run certain jobs up to 200 times faster than other computers of its time, according to accounts of its capabilities.According to a report by IEEE Spectrum, Harvest finally stopped running on February 27, 1976, after a mechanical component in its automated tape library wore out. The manufacturer of the part was no longer in business, leaving the NSA without a practical way to replace it. By then, the machine had operated through the Cuban Missile Crisis, the Vietnam War, and the period leading up to the 1975 Helsinki Accords.Harvest was officially designated the IBM 7950 and was built around IBM's 7030 Stretch mainframe. IBM developed Stretch for scientific computing, but the NSA needed a system that could continuously process large volumes of intercepted communications without requiring operators to manually stage each batch of tape.After two unsuccessful proposals, IBM secured the NSA contract in 1958. The resulting system combined Stretch with a custom streaming processor and an automated tape-storage system called Tractor.Unlike a general-purpose computer, Harvest's custom processor was designed to repeatedly apply a fixed sequence of operations to data streams. It could take two streams, known as P and Q, from memory, process them and return the result as a third stream, R.The processor used overlapping stages, or a pipeline, so that while one pair of data bytes was being processed, the next could already be fetched from memory. Harvest shared memory with Stretch and could address individual bits rather than being restricted to complete bytes or words.Its processing units included a logic unit for bitwise operations and a table-lookup unit that could use incoming data to address information in memory.The NSA used Harvest for cryptanalytic and large-scale text-processing jobs. One documented example described the machine searching 3.5 billion characters of text for any of 7,000 target terms in just under four hours.Another job, referred to asinvolved searching 11 million messages covering 16 years of intercepted traffic against about 8,000 search terms. NSA analyst Robert Looney said in 1972 that the job took about 10 hours, although he did not disclose the purpose of the search.As a complete system, Harvest could stream one byte every 0.3 microseconds and had about 800 kilobytes of addressable memory.IBM engineer Frances Allen, who worked on both Stretch and Harvest, later recalled the type of operations the machine could perform.Allen said in a 2001 oral history.Harvest's specialised design also created challenges within the NSA. According to James Bamford's 2001 history of the agency, some officials reportedly looked at the machine during employee tours and said,The system nonetheless continued to handle large jobs that general-purpose machines were not well suited to process.Harvest's processing capacity required a storage system that could supply large datasets without constant human intervention. IBM therefore built Tractor, an automated magnetic-tape library officially designated the IBM 7955.Each Tractor cassette weighed about 6 to 7 kilograms and contained roughly 120 megabytes of data on a 550-metre reel of tape. Each storage unit could hold up to 160 cassettes.When Harvest began operating in 1962, three automatic cartridge units were connected to it, each serving two tape drives. Together, they provided about 44 gigabytes of online storage.The automated system used a motor-driven arm to retrieve cassettes from storage racks and deliver them to tape drives. The mechanism could move at about 6 metres per second, while software running on Stretch controlled cassette movement and data reading and writing.Moving from one completed tape to the next could take about 18 seconds, once the next cassette had been retrieved and was ready to mount. Retrieving and preparing a cassette did not require manual handling.Tractor therefore functioned as both long-term storage and a source of data for Harvest's processing jobs. Conventional reel-to-reel drives connected to Stretch were also used when large datasets had to be transferred into or out of the system.IBM and the NSA also developed a programming language specifically for Harvest. Called Alpha, short for Advanced Language for Programming Harvest, it was designed around the machine's streaming architecture and the needs of cryptanalysts.Alpha allowed programmers to define the alphabet used for cryptographic data and included symbols for representing uncertain or null characters. Arepresented by a question mark, indicated a character that was known to exist but whose identity was unknown. A blank space represented aor null character.The language also provided ways to combine strings into larger structures, giving programmers a way to describe complex intercepted messages and cryptanalytic datasets.Allen worked on the Harvest software and later recalled that the technical report she produced for her part of the project disappeared into the NSA's classified system after she completed it.she recalled in 2001.Harvest's secrecy also shaped how some IBM employees understood the project. Allen said the NSA was not widely known outside classified intelligence circles when she began working on the machine, so she initially believed she was working on a naval project. The budget code name for the NSA wasBy 1971, Harvest was operating about 115 hours a week, according to Looney, representing more than two-thirds of its available operating time. At the same time, the number of jobs it handled had been declining since 1967 as newer general-purpose computers took over ordinary data-processing work.Harvest was increasingly reserved for large, specialised workloads that other machines could not handle as efficiently.At the system's 10th anniversary in 1972, Looney described it as a machineThe description did not last much longer.On February 27, 1976, operators shut Harvest down for the final time. A mechanical component in the Tractor tape library had worn out, and the company that manufactured the part was no longer operating. Replacing the system's ageing hardware was no longer practical.The NSA marked the occasion with a mock telegram written in Harvest's name.it said.The NSA eventually replaced Harvest with the Cray-1 supercomputer. Unlike Harvest, the Cray-1 used newer integrated circuits and was designed primarily for numerical and scientific computing, but its processing capabilities also made it suitable for workloads that had previously required Harvest's specialised hardware.The Cray-1 was also commercially available to multiple customers, unlike Harvest, which had been built specifically for the NSA. As newer general-purpose and scientific systems improved, maintaining a custom machine for one specialised workload became less practical.Harvest did not have a direct line of successors, partly because its architecture was built around the NSA's particular requirements. Several of its concepts, however, appeared later in other areas of computing.Tractor's automated tape library anticipated robotic storage systems later used in large data centres. Harvest's pipeline architecture also resembled approaches that became part of dataflow computing, while its continuous pattern-matching operations have parallels in later systems designed to inspect network traffic.Harvest's operational life ended with a worn mechanical part and an unavailable manufacturer, but the ideas used to build the system continued to appear in computing systems developed after it.
Article Summary: IBM built a secret computer for the US National Security Agency that began operating in 1962 and remained in service for 14 years. Known as Harvest, the machine could run certain jobs up to 200 times faster than other computers of its time. One documented example described the machine searching 3.5 billion characters of text for any of 7,000 target terms.
